title: Apportioned streaming concession model pilot for asymmetric I/O billing
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: enterprise customers and high-throughput conversational products show very different input/output token ratios. Our current minimums and streaming concessions (flat streaming grace credits) overcharge interactive read-heavy agents and under-incentivize efficient ingress-heavy batch jobs. Goal: design a short pilot that applies a proportional (apportioned) concession to streaming minimums based on measured input:output token distribution, validate the business and technical impact, gather telemetry, and collect Enterprise SQ/legal feedback for contract language.

Scope: hosted API only; opt-in test cohort of up to 15 customers (mix of mid-market and enterprise); two-week synthetic simulation followed by a four-week live pilot; metrics to track cost delta, revenue delta, customer satisfaction, and fraud/abuse signals.

Non-goals: changing reserved capacity pricing, dedicated contracts, or embedding pricing rules for private deployments in this pilot.
acceptance_criteria: Define formula for apportioned concession: concession = base_streaming_credit * apportioned_factor where apportioned_factor = output_tokens / (input_tokens + output_tokens) clamped to [0.2,0.9] (documented)
Instrument telemetry: token counts by direction per request, session-scoped aggregation, tag by customer and route (done in backend and surfaced to console)
Run offline simulation against 30 days of anonymized production traces and produce per-customer P&L & billing delta report
Select and enroll 10-15 customers for opt-in pilot with legal-approved amendment language
No customer should see >20% unexpected monthly billing delta without explicit opt-in and notice
Security and Legal sign-off on enterprise SQ implications and contract wording
Experiment dashboard with daily P&L, unit economics, and customer-level alerts available to PM and finance
decisions: Use proportional apportioning based on observed token split (output-weighted) instead of a fixed directional floor
Clamp apportioned factor to avoid extremes (min 20% output credit, max 90%) to prevent gaming and protect throughput-heavy customers
Pilot will be opt-in and include explicit billing preview emails 7 days before changes take effect
Telemetry will be emitted under telemetry.v1.pricing.apportioned_streaming with tags: customer_id, route, model, sequence_length_percentiles
links_to_artifacts: Simulation workbook (sheets): per-customer delta, cohort aggregation, sensitivity analysis
GA-runbook: how to revert concession for a customer

risks: Revenue leakage for high-output customers if bounds are poorly tuned
Gaming risk: clients could manipulate token split via prompting or padding to maximize concessions
Telemetry volume increase impacting ingestion pipeline costs
Enterprise SQ/legal may require additional auditability that increases engineering scope
mitigations: Clamp apportioned factor to conservative bounds and iterate after 2 weeks of live telemetry
Add heuristics to detect abrupt shifts in token ratios per session and surface for manual review
Rate-limit telemetry emissions for pilot customers and batch metrics before upstreaming
Include explicit contract language about measurement windows and dispute resolution in amendment
rollout_plan: Week 0: internal simulation and finance sign-off
Week 1: telemetry and gating flag deployed to canary; QA + performance benchmarks
Week 2-3: opt-in pilot with 12 customers; daily dashboard and weekly sync with legal/finance
Week 4: evaluate metrics; decide on scale, tweak clamps, or roll back
Post-pilot: compile learnings and propose either A) staged rollout with cohort expansion B) cancel and document findings
